title: Stabilization Playbook + 30‑Day Ops Calendar (Aug 2026) - Draft
content:
Summary:
This doc is a compact stabilization playbook and 30‑day operations calendar for releases where we anticipate nontrivial traffic pattern changes (model swaps, routing policy updates, or capacity rebalancing). Goal: give release leads and oncall teams a prioritized checklist and time-boxed calendar for the first 30 days after cutover so we can catch regressions early and roll forward/back safely.

Status and scope:
- Draft: internal circulation only.
- Applies to: hosted API releases, Dedicated capacity migrations, and Private control-plane upgrades that change routing or model variants.
- Assumes normal cutover playbook already executed (preflight checks, blue/green or canary steps). This focuses on stabilization and medium-term validation.

Quick decision heuristics (TL;DR):
- If p99 response latency increases >20% for >30m and correlates with a single region -> consider immediate partial rollback to previous routing policy for that region.
- If user-visible error rate (>=5xx) doubles baseline for >15m -> trigger incident bridge and default fallback model.
- If latency increases but cost decreases and error rates are stable -> evaluate with product before rolling back (may accept for now).

30‑Day Ops Calendar (high level, week-by-week checkpoints):
W0 (cutover day):
  - 00:00–02:00 post-cutover: smoke tests (automated + manual), sample traces for top 10 routes (see 'Telemetry quick checks').
  - 02:00–06:00: monitoring watch (oncall + release lead); short handoff notes every 2 hours via #release-ops.
  - 06:00–24:00: rolling checks every 4 hours; first 1000 customer requests manually reviewed for edge-cases.
  - Deliverable: first-cut release notes posted in #releases and product email draft ready.
W1 (stabilize):
  - Daily 09:30 sync (15m) between oncall, infra, and release lead (standup notes in this doc).
  - Run A/B traffic split analysis at 24h and 72h.
  - Complete smoke-run of upgrade-specific regressions (regression suite id: RDW-regen-03).
  - Telemetry audit at day 3 (see panel list).
W2 (validate correctness):
  - Quality evals against 5 canonical prompt sets (owner: Applied ML).
  - Check customer feedback queue for new issues; categorize by severity.
  - Begin throttled expansion of dedicated capacity (if applicable).
W3 (cost & perf tuning):
  - Run batching/quantization tuning suggestions from Redwood Optimize for the new model variant.
  - Evaluate autoscaling events; adjust policy if sustained 5min CPU or GPU saturation observed.
W4 (rollforward decision):
  - Final decision checkpoint: keep release as-is / patch / rollback.
  - If keep: produce 'release-stable' tag + update changelog and SDK docs.
  - If rollback: use rollback playbook (section below) and schedule immediate postmortem.

Primary checklists (actionable items, ordered by priority)
A) Immediate post-cutover (first 6 hours)
  - [ ] Confirm traffic routing matched planned percentages (grafana panel: Routing/TrafficSplit).
  - [ ] Validate latency p50/p90/p99 against pre-cutover baselines. Query: latency_api.server.response_ms{route=~"top.*"}.
  - [ ] Confirm checksum/version for runtime binary and model artifacts on each pod.
  - [ ] Run smoke inference on 20 sample prompts across languages. Record output diffs.
  - [ ] Verify KV-cache warmup: 95th percentile cold-start token latency below threshold.
  - [ ] Post initial release notes stub to #releases channel.

B) Critical telemetry checks (first 72 hours)
  - [ ] Error rate by endpoint (5xx, model-timeouts). Threshold: <0.5% overall, <1% for any single route.
  - [ ] Model hallucination signals (eval classifier): if false_positive_rate increases >10% from baseline, tag for ML review.
  - [ ] GPU temperature and memory OOM events: none allowed for Dedicated.
  - [ ] KV cache hit ratio: expected >80% for conversational workloads.
  - [ ] Backend queue length: ensure <10ms processing tail.

C) Customer-impact synthesis (ongoing)
  - [ ] Compile top-5 customer errors daily into a single digest (owner: Customer Success).
  - [ ] Flag any regressions that affect SLA customers immediately to account exec and solutions eng.
  - [ ] For any API contract change, publish migration steps and compatibility notes on console and SDK CHANGELOG.

Rollback and fast-fallback plan (condensed)
  - Trigger conditions (any of): sustained p99 >1.5x baseline for 30m; unresolvable 5xx spike for 15m; data-safety alert.
  - Rollback types: soft-fallback (route subset to previous model variant) vs full rollback (re-deploy previous release).
  - Soft-fallback procedure (preferred when region-specific):
    1) Update routing rule: set previous model weight to 80% for afflicted region.
    2) Monitor error signal and user complaints for 10 minutes.
    3) If stable, gradually expand fallback to 100% over 30m, then schedule full rollback during low-traffic window.
  - Full rollback checklist:
    - [ ] Create incident bridge and notify #incident and #release-ops.
    - [ ] Block new deployments to impacted pools.
    - [ ] Redeploy prior image and model tag, then run preflight smoke.
    - [ ] Post rollback notes and schedule postmortem.

Telemetry quick checks (shortcut commands / dashboard names)
  - Grafana panels: "API Latency by Route", "Routing Traffic Split", "Model Error Rate", "KV Cache Hit Ratio", "GPU Utilization per Pod".
  - Logs: grep for "runtime:panic" and "model:timeout" across the last 30m.
  - Traces: sample 25 traces for top 3 failing routes; look for excessive kernel waits or network retries.
  - SLI queries (examples):
    - success_rate = sum(rate(http_requests_total{code!~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))
    - p99_latency_ms = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) * 1000

Communications templates (short)
  - Incident preface (Slack post): "Release RDW-1423: partial rollback initiated for region us-west-2 due to p99 latency regression. Teams on bridge: @oncall-frontend @infra @applied-ml. ETA: first stabilization signal in 30m. See bridge: <link>."
  - Customer-facing note (for high-impact): "We observed higher-than-normal latency for a subset of requests in region X and applied a rollback to restore expected performance. No data loss reported. Full update and remediation timeline will follow."

Release notes draft (to cut-and-paste into product channel)
Version: 2026.8.12-RDW1423 (draft)
Short summary: Incremental routing and model variant updates to improve latency tradeoffs and reduce cost per token for medium-length prompts.
Key changes:
  - Model: switch to rwd-llama-70b-q8 (quantized) with optimized kernels for Ampere/Neoverse.
  - Routing: dynamic-cost routing enabled for standard tier; fallback model pinned for enterprise.
  - Observability: added p99 tail traces and model-level token accounting in console.
Known issues (tracked):
  - In rare conversational threads, token truncation observed for >12% of test prompts -> temporary mitigation: increase max-window for affected tenants.
  - Some SDK versions (v1.3.0) may surface schema warnings for function-calling payloads (workaround: upgrade to v1.3.2).
Migration notes for partners:
  - No API contract changes; recommend clients use streaming endpoints where latency-sensitive.
  - If you maintain on-prem deployments, refer to Private release notes PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/519

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- Should we add a daily synthetic workload that emulates small-batch chat bursts? (ask applied-ml)
- Who owns the 'first 1000 requests manual review'? (pending: Benji and CS)
- Add runbook hooks to automatically snapshot heap/core dumps for top-failure pods.

Post-release artifacts to produce before 'stable' tag:
- Compiled evaluation report (applied-ml).
- Cost delta analysis and per-route unit economics (finance + infra).
- Customer impact digest and support ticket taxonomy (customer-success).

Appendix: quick-links and playbook snippets
- Preflight checklist reference: Confluence: Launch Checklist Template (linked above).
- Rollback script: ops/deploy/rollback.sh -- dry-run flag available.
- Canaries to watch: /routes/chat/stream, /routes/generate/bulk, /routes/embeddings/text-sim

Notes: This doc intentionally mixes tactical checklists and calendar entries — keep concise and actionable. Feedback welcome; will fold into canonical release runbook v2 after this release window.
